diseases.name: Wheat Rust / Stripe Rust
diseases.symptoms: Yellow to orange blister-like lesions arranged in stripes on leaves. Severe infections cause premature defoliation and shriveled grains.
diseases.treatment: Use rust-resistant varieties (e.g., HD 2967, PBW 723). For chemical treatment, foliar sprays of Propiconazole 25 EC or Tebuconazole 25 EC are standard, but consult ICAR/local authorities for exact dosage and timing.

sources.organization: ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research
sources.title: Wheat Disease Management

diseases.name: Late Blight
diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked irregular spots on leaves that turn brown/black. White cottony growth on the underside during humid weather. Rapid necrosis of vines.
diseases.treatment: Ensure proper drainage and use healthy seed tubers. Preventative sprays of Mancozeb 75 WP or systemic fungicides like Metalaxyl are recommended. Consult ICAR-CPRI guidelines for exact dosage.

sources.title: Late Blight of Potato and its Management

diseases.name: Fall Armyworm
diseases.symptoms: Larvae feed on leaves causing ragged holes, often leaving sawdust-like frass in the whorl. Severe defoliation and feeding on developing ears.
diseases.treatment: Early scouting is critical. Use whorl application of sand + lime or neem seed kernel extract (NSKE) 5% for organic management. Chemical options include Emamectin benzoate or Spinetoram. Consult ICAR-IIMR for exact dosage.

diseases.name: Rice Blast
diseases.symptoms: Diamond-shaped or spindle-shaped lesions with gray centers and brown margins on leaves. Can also affect nodes and panicles (neck blast), causing panicle lodging.
diseases.treatment: Avoid excessive nitrogen application. Delay draining the field. Chemical options include Tricyclazole 75 WP or Isoprothiolane 40 EC. Consult ICAR-IIRR for exact dosage.

diseases.name: Bacterial Leaf Blight
diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked to yellowish stripes on leaf blades or starting at leaf tips, later enlarging and turning pale yellow to grayish white. Leaves wilt and roll up.
diseases.treatment: Use resistant varieties. Avoid excess nitrogen. Chemical control is often ineffective; prevention is key. Copper fungicides may provide limited suppression. Consult ICAR-IIRR for specific recommendations.
